_comment: Calibration fixture for the spec-005 error-message-quality judge.
Every `good` case is REAL output captured from fastskill 0.9.179 by running the
command shown. Nothing here is an invented example of what a good message might
look like -- the judge has to agree with humans about messages the product
actually emits, not about idealised prose.
The `bad` cases are messages fastskill could realistically regress into. Three are
historical: `clap_duplicate_arg_panic` is the panic that `fastskill init` really
produced before PR #225 (an arg named `version` collided with clap's generated
--version), `unwrap_panic` is the shape any stray .unwrap() produces, and
`repos_skills_unknown_argument` is what `repos skills nosuchrepo` really produced
before it gained a positional REPOSITORY arg. They are reconstructed rather than
captured because the bugs are fixed -- which is the point: the judge exists to catch
`expected.pass` is the human verdict and is what calibration scores against.
`expected.score_range` is advisory -- exact scores vary between reasonable judges,
so agreement is measured on pass/fail, with score used only to spot a judge that
gets the verdict right for visibly wrong reasons.
Keep this set BALANCED. A fixture that is mostly `pass` can be gamed by a judge
that always answers `pass`, and would report ~80% agreement while being useless.

cases.output:
Error: Skill 'no-such-skill' not found

Searched locations:
  ✓ /tmp/proj/skills (project)

Try:
  fastskill install owner/repo
  fastskill list                    # See available skills

expected.why: Names the specific missing skill, shows where it looked so the user can tell whether the path was wrong, and offers two concrete next commands. Clean, no internals. Exit 1 is right.

cases.output: Error: Validation error: No SKILL.md found in ./does-not-exist. A skill directory must contain a SKILL.md file. If this folder has multiple skills in subdirectories, use --recursive.

expected.why: Names the path, states the requirement that was violated, and anticipates the most likely cause with a specific flag to fix it.

cases.output:
Error: Skill 'ghost' not found

Searched locations:
  ✓ /tmp/proj/skills (project)

Try:
  fastskill install owner/repo
  fastskill list                    # See available skills

expected.why: Same shape as read_not_found. Included deliberately: a judge that scores identical messages inconsistently is not usable, so this is a self-consistency probe.

cases.output:
Installing skills...

Error: Configuration error: skill-project.toml validation failed: Project-level skill-project.toml (at project root) requires [dependencies] section. Add '[dependencies]' section to manage skill dependencies. Use 'fastskill add <skill-id>' to add skills.

expected.why: Says exactly which section is missing from which file and gives both a manual fix and a command. Slightly jargon-heavy ('validation failed') and the nested prefixes are clumsy, so a 3 is defensible -- but it is actionable, which is what pass turns on.

cases.output: error[E004]: invalid value 'notanumber' for 'limit'; expected integer

expected.why: Names the offending value, the field, and the expected type. Terse and offers no next command, but a user knows precisely what to change.

cases.output:
error[E002]: unknown argument
  hint: Use --help to see available arguments
Error: unknown argument

expected.why: HISTORICAL, not current: this was the real output before `repos skills` grew a positional REPOSITORY arg (fastskill-cli/src/commands/repos.rs) and main.rs stopped double-printing already-reported UsageErrors. `nosuchrepo` now resolves to `Repository 'nosuchrepo' not found`. Kept, like clap_duplicate_arg_panic below, as a regression fixture -- the judge should still fail this exact shape if the parser path regresses.

cases.output:
thread 'main' panicked at /root/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-6f17d22bba15001f/clap_builder-4.5.23/src/builder/debug_asserts.rs:99:13:
Command init: Argument names must be unique, but 'version' is in use by more than one argument or group
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace

expected.why: The panic `fastskill init` really produced before PR #225. Raw Rust panic with a vendored crate path and an internal invariant. Says nothing the user can act on -- it is not even their fault. Exit 101 signals a crash, not a usage error.

cases.output:
thread 'main' panicked at crates/fastskill-core/src/core/manifest.rs:412:38:
called `Option::unwrap()` on a `None` value
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace

expected.why: The shape any stray .unwrap() produces. Leaks a source path and line, names no user-facing problem, offers no action.

The canonical useless error. Correct exit code and no internals leaked, so a judge weighing only cleanliness might wave it through -- which is exactly the failure mode this case exists to detect. Zero specificity, zero actionability.

cases.output: Error: data did not match any variant of untagged enum DependencySpec

expected.why: REAL historical output: what a pre-Origin manifest produced before the migration hint. Technically accurate and completely unactionable -- it names an internal Rust type, not the file, line, or field the user must change.
